item.title: On Fujita's Advanced Generalized Mukai Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Fujita's advanced generalized Mukai conjecture for smooth complex Fano varieties. Our starting point is the existence of independent two-point Gromov--Witten correspondences. We show that there are finitely many unsplit families of rational curves whose chains connect $X$. We use these families to bound the anticanonical degrees throughout the successive minimal horizontal construction, so every family in that construction is unsplit. Fujita's contraction theorem and inductive classification then give the required list of varieties.
item.dc:creator: Duo Li

item.title: A motivic Vojta inequality for non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded height
item.description: arXiv:2611.05672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a bounded-degree form of a motivic Vojta inequality for pure Andr\'e motives, arising from a question of Kato. We verify this inequality for infinitely many non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded stable Faltings height. The point is that ramification at the finite poles of the $j$-invariant gives the required discriminant bound.
item.dc:creator: Daiki Kawabe

item.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles. Over the complex numbers, and for G connected reductive, this lifts Grojnowski's theory from the moduli space of G-bundles to the stack. The key player is the category of perfect complexes on A with 0-dimensional support, equipped with the convolution product induced by the group law of A. It plays the role of a categorified circle and is used to define a loop space $L_A^G(X)$, whose structure sheaf gives rise to $H_A^G(X)$ after periodization. Sheaves on $L_A^G(X)$ equivariant under loop rotation provide a category of coefficients for $H_A^G(-)$ in the same way that D-modules provide coefficients for de Rham cohomology. At the point X = *, the theory also gives rise to an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum (or sheaf thereof) $K_A$, which recovers complex K-theory for $A = \mathbf{G}_m$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}^{top}$ of topological modular forms for the universal elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Emile Bouaziz, Adeel A. Khan

item.title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
item.description: arXiv:2611.05809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface. We obtain an explicit degree bound depending on a projective embedding. We apply this construction to a cyclic cover compactification associated with a smooth Campana orbifold $(X,\sum_i(1-1/m_i)D_i)$. If its anticanonical divisor is big, we show that there is a covering family of free divisible Campana rational curves with fixed numerical class and contact data. In Picard number one case, the orbifold is Campana rationally connected.
item.dc:creator: Jiun-Cheng Chen, Hsian-Hua Tseng

item.title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted. When $d$ divides $M$, the Kuznetsov component is a Calabi--Yau category, as for cubic fourfolds, where categorical Torelli is known to fail. We show that, apart from cubic fourfolds, such a hypersurface has a number of Fourier--Mukai partners bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $M$, and that categorical Torelli holds in sufficiently large degree, in every dimension. The main tool is a deformation theorem: when geometric deformations surject onto the second Hochschild cohomology of the Kuznetsov components, an equivalence deforms together with the hypersurfaces, so statements proved for general hypersurfaces extend to all smooth ones.
item.dc:creator: Xun Lin, Shizhuo Zhang

item.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $\lambda_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(\lambda_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bishop

item.title: Capelli Operators and the Bernstein-Sato polynomials of Minors
item.description: arXiv:2611.06030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every ideal of minors of a generic complex matrix, we determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial. These roots lie in explicit rational intervals indexed by the rank strata. Every nonintegral root is simple, whereas the multiplicity of each integral root equals the number of labels producing that root. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture, including the inequality relating pole orders to root multiplicities; for minors of size $r$, the largest possible root multiplicity over all matrix dimensions is $\lfloor\sqrt{4r-1}\rfloor$. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Chen, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
item.description: arXiv:2611.06077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves. In this paper, we determine the parity of the intersection forms of all fake quadrics isogenous to a product of unmixed type. In particular, we show that there are fake quadrics with odd intersection forms.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Catanese, JongHae Keum, Do Geun Kim, Kyoung-Seog Lee

item.title: PCF All The Way Down
item.description: arXiv:2611.06106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhouran Wang

item.title: A general L\^e--Siersma formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.06340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of L\^e and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.
item.dc:creator: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, J. J. Nu\~no-Ballesteros

item.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an algorithm for enumerating ordinary K3 surfaces over a fixed finite field based on Taelman's theorem. We use this algorithm to prove that there exist no K3 surfaces without rational points over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 13$. For elliptic K3 surfaces, we give a geometric proof of this non-existence without computer assistance. On the other hand, we also provide explicit pointless K3 surfaces over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\leq 11$.
item.dc:creator: Simon Brandhorst, Yuta Takada

item.title: On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.06398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.
item.dc:creator: Rui Tan, Fanghan Xiang

item.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.06621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Huang, Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Puddu

item.title: Hessenberg character
item.description: arXiv:2611.06852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Brosnan, Jaehyun Hong, Donggun Lee

item.title: The pliability of del Pezzo surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $G$-Mori fibre space models of $G$-del Pezzo surfaces, focusing on surfaces over non-closed fields. We construct explicit examples of birationally rigid sextic del Pezzo surfaces and give a negative answer to a generalization of Koll\'ar's question on birational rigidity and field extensions: a sextic del Pezzo surface of Picard rank $1$ can fail to be birationally rigid over its ground field but become birationally rigid after an algebraic field extension. We interpret this phenomenon in terms of the failure of injectivity of natural maps in nonabelian Galois cohomology induced by the inclusion of automorphism groups into birational automorphism groups. We also show that finite pliability is unbounded: for every integer $d\geqslant2$, we construct a sextic del Pezzo surface of index $3$ over a field of characteristic zero whose pliability is exactly $3^d+1$.
item.dc:creator: Elias Kurz, Egor Yasinsky

item.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $\Phi(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).
item.dc:creator: Giordano Cotti

item.title: Representations of 3D Rotations: Mathematical Foundations and Comparative Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2605.08086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rotation representations are foundational in fields such as computer graphics, robotics, and machine learning, where precise and efficient modeling of 3D orientations is critical. This paper comprehensively investigates diverse representations of the special orthogonal group $SO(3)$, such as Euler angles, axis-angle vectors, quaternions, rotation matrices, exponential maps, and emerging continuous and probabilistic methods, evaluating their mathematical formulations, continuity, susceptibility to gimbal lock, computational efficiency, storage requirements, interpolation properties, and composition operations, while integrating detailed algebraic insights with practical applications in fields like animation, pose estimation, inertial navigation, 3D shape registration, and neural networks. Empirical evidence highlights quaternions' dominance due to their compactness and computational efficiency, while alternatives like 6D continuous representations and matrix Fisher distributions provide enhanced continuity and uncertainty modeling. Future research could explore hybrid methods and thorough large-scale evaluations to help build a solid foundation for improving rotation representation techniques.
item.dc:creator: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Haochen Liu, James Hahn

item.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.05526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rayan, Evan Sundbo

item.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.05679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Lu

item.title: A toric approach to social choice theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.
item.dc:creator: Ata Poyraz Turna, Ben Y. Wormleighton

item.title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.05905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Giannini

item.title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
item.description: arXiv:2611.05914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Shibuta

item.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2611.06193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.
item.dc:creator: Ankita Das

item.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.
item.dc:creator: Yixuan Fu

item.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2611.06370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.
item.dc:creator: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Steven Dale Cutkosky

item.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Fei Yu, Junming Zhang

item.title: Uniform localization and boundary corrections for two-node quiver Coulomb branches
item.description: arXiv:2611.06509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct simple coherent classes and compute their normalized difference operators for the two-node quiver Coulomb branch with gauge group $GL_1\times GL_2$ and $m-1$ framing columns at the second node. The first magnetic charge is fixed at zero. For every $m\geq1$, every support $(n,-1)$ with $n\geq1$, and every integral electric twist, we prove that termwise saturation of the matter Koszul complex gives the simple intermediate extension. A graded normalization formula expresses its localization on every stratum as a finite binomial shuffle sum. The resulting operators satisfy bar symmetry, positive bubbling order, paired root-residue cancellation, and integral Laurent polynomial action. For $m=4$, we construct the derived boundary correction on $(2,-2)$, retaining the nonsemisimple odd-electric boundary object, and compute all electric twists. Finally, matter Euler divisibility proves triangular uniqueness on arbitrary fixed rank-two magnetic supports inside the actual integral Coulomb image. A pole-free counterexample shows why residue conditions alone do not give this uniqueness. Existence on general deeper mixed-sign supports remains open.
item.dc:creator: Xiaomin Tang

item.title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.06675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.
item.dc:creator: Chenglang Yang, Xuhui Zhang

item.title: Algebraicity of the image of period map
item.description: arXiv:1608.06029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the image of period map is algebraic, as conjectured by Griffiths.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

item.title: Birational geometry of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2507.21737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the biregular and birational geometry of degree 6 del Pezzo surfaces with Picard number 1, defined over an arbitrary perfect field. Using Galois cohomology techniques, we obtain an explicit description of cocycles for such surfaces and describe the Severi-Brauer varieties associated with them, recovering the biregular classification of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. We then compute the automorphism groups of such surfaces, describe their closed points in general position and investigate the structure of Sarkisov links at such points and the corresponding birational models, answering a question of M. Rost. Using this description, we show that degree 6 del Pezzo surfaces are the only solid surfaces that admit infinite pliability. We also find a system of generators and relations for the groups of birational transformations of such surfaces and use it to construct nontrivial quotients of these groups, including free groups on uncountable sets.
item.dc:creator: Elias Kurz, Egor Yasinsky

item.title: Curve semistable Higgs bundles and smooth projective varieties whose canonical bundle is ample
item.description: arXiv:2508.12062v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Considering the so-called Simpson system on smooth projective varieties, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, whose canonical bundle is ample, we provide a new proof of the stability of this Higgs bundle, which in turn yields another proof of the Miyaoka-Yau inequality. When equality holds, we prove that the discriminant class of the Simpson system is numerically trivial and that this Higgs bundle is curve semistable. This result follows from a study of the relations between weak ampleness, numerically effectiveness for Higgs bundles that ``feel'' the Higgs field and (semi)stability. Moreover, we obtain another proof of the algebraic hyperbolicity of these varieties which provides a lower bound on a positive real constant related to this property; to best of our knowledge, this is the first and only result of this type. We conjecture that a similar lower bound holds for smooth projective varieties whose canonical bundle is ample.
item.dc:creator: Armando Capasso

item.title: Derived isogenies between abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2510.22612v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a derived Torelli Theorem for twisted abelian varieties. Starting from this, we explore the relation between derived isogenies and classical isogenies. We show that two abelian varieties of dimension $\geq 2$ are derived isogenous if and only if they are principally isogenous over fields of characteristic zero. This generalized the result for abelian surfaces and completely solves the question raised in [arXiv:2108.08710].
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Li, Ziwei Lu, Zhichao Tang

item.title: Embedded topological triviality of separable families of singularities
item.description: arXiv:2511.23185v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding how singularities behave under small perturbations is a central theme in singularity theory. In this paper, we study separable families $f_s=f_0+\rho(s)\varphi$ of analytic function-germs on a germ of a complex analytic space $(X,0)$, and we give sufficient conditions for them to admit a topological trivialization. Our results extend previous work by the third author and collaborators, moving from abstract triviality to the embedded setting. As an application, we obtain new instances of topological stability, including a class of $\mu$-constant deformations. These findings provide a new perspective on the long-standing $\mu$-constant conjecture, one of the major open problems in the field.
item.dc:creator: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, Andreas Lind, Aur\'elio Menegon

item.title: Derived Hodge-to-de Rham Degeneration and Quasihomogeneous Curve Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2604.05825v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Hodge-completed derived Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of integral projective complex curves. We prove E2-degeneration whenever every singularity is analytically quasihomogeneous, without a local complete intersection (lci) hypothesis. An explicit lci counterexample shows that the converse fails in general. For lci curves, E2-degeneration bounds the total Milnor-Tjurina defect by the dimension of the space of global Kahler one-forms modulo torsion, and hence by the genus of the normalization. This yields a converse for lci curves whose global Kahler one-forms are all torsion, including those with rational normalization. We also establish the converse for locally planar curves. An example with elliptic normalization shows that the numerical defect bound alone is not sufficient for E2-degeneration, even when equality holds.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan He, Junxiao Wang

item.title: Weierstrass semigroups at totally ramified places of degree one on generalized Kummer extensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.14583v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explicitly describe the set of gaps and the Weierstrass semigroup at a totally ramified place of degree one on a generalized Kummer extension defined by the affine equation $y^m = f(x)$ over $K$, an algebraic extension of $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $f(x)\in K(x)$ and $K$ is not required to contain a primitive $m$-th root of unity. For the different totally ramified places of degree one, our description takes a unified form. Then we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for the Weierstrass semigroup at a totally ramified place of degree one to be symmetric. Furthermore, we investigate the minimal generating set of the Weierstrass semigroups at many totally ramified places of degree one. We not only explicitly describe the minimal generating set, but also provide functions whose coefficients of pole divisors lie in the minimal generating set. Finally, we apply our results to generalized Kummer extensions with the same multiplicities, as well as function fields of GGS curves and subcovers of the BM curve.
item.dc:creator: Huachao Zhang, Chang-An Zhao

item.title: Categorical genus for log del Pezzo surfaces with cyclic quotient singularities
item.description: arXiv:2609.13102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(X\) be a log del Pezzo surface with cyclic quotient singularities and \(\mathcal{X}\) its canonical stack. We define the categorical genus of \(\mathcal{X}\) as half the rank of its antisymmetric numerical Euler pairing. Using Serre duality and inertial Riemann--Roch, we compute \[ g_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal{X})=1+\frac{1}{2}\sum_j w_j(\ell_j-1), \] where \(w_j\) and \(\ell_j\) are the local widths and Gorenstein indices of the singularities, and identify the local contributions with twisted sectors of age less than one. We determine how categorical genus changes under general \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein deformation and express the resulting decrease in terms of the smoothable \(T\)-content. When \(X\) admits a toric \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein degeneration, the categorical genus of a general deformation agrees with Tveiten's mutable genus, given by the residual interior lattice points of the corresponding Fano polygon. Under additional hypotheses, we recover this genus formula through the singularities of compactified mirror curves.
item.dc:creator: Alex Junior Gomez Saltachin

item.title: Projective blowups: a formal and multicentered proof
item.description: arXiv:2609.28489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a machine-checked proof, in Lean 4, of the universal property of multi- centered blowups: given a finite family Z of closed subschemes of a scheme X, presented on each chart by ideals, there is a scheme BlZ X over X, terminal among X-schemes on which every member of the family becomes an effective Cartier divisor. To the best of our knowledge this is the first formalisation of blowups, single- or multicentered, in any theorem prover. The proof is organised around the universal property of the multicentered dilatation of a ring. The comparison isomorphisms on overlaps, the cocycle identity, and the independence of the chosen presentation are obtained from the uniqueness part of this universal property. We give the exact theorem statement as formalized, the proof architecture, and the main new mathematical ingredients, together with the corresponding Lean code.
item.dc:creator: A. Mayeux

item.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Dmitrii Pavlov, Rainer Sinn

item.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.00864v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: Prime order torsion on elliptic curves over number fields. Part I: Asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2505.14109v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotics of the set $S(d)$ of possible prime orders of $K$-rational points on elliptic curves over number fields $K$ of degree $d$ as $d$ tends to infinity. Assuming some conjectures on the sparsity of newforms of weight $2$ and prime level with unexpectedly high analytic rank, we show that $\max S(d) \le 3d + 1$ for sufficiently large even $d$ and $\max S(d) = o(d)$ for odd $d$. This gives a significant (but conjectural) improvement on the currently best known upper bound $\max S(d) \le (3^{d/2} + 1)^2$ due to Oesterl\'e.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Derickx, Michael Stoll

item.title: Noncommutative marked surfaces II: tagged triangulations, clusters, and their symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2507.20393v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The aim of the paper is to define noncommutative cluster structure on several algebras ${\mathcal A}$ related to marked surfaces possibly with orbifold points of various orders, which includes noncommutative clusters, i.e., embeddings of a given group $G$ into the multiplicative monoid ${\mathcal A}^\times$ and an action of a certain braid-like group $Br_{\mathcal A}$ by automorphisms of each cluster group in a compatible way. For punctured surfaces we construct new symmetries, noncommutative tagged clusters and establish a noncommutative Laurent Phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Arkady Berenstein, Min Huang, Vladimir Retakh

item.title: On the de Rham flip-flopping in dual towers
item.description: arXiv:2603.07869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a version of de Rham and Hyodo-Kato flip-flopping for dual towers of rigid analytic spaces including those coming from dual basic local Shimura varieties. The main tool are comparison theorems expressing the two cohomologies as pro-\'etale cohomology of corresponding relative period sheaves that, by definition, satisfy pro-\'etale descent. As an application, we show that de Rham and Hyodo-Kato cohomologies of finite level coverings of the Drinfeld space of any dimension $d$ over $K$ are admissible as representations of $\mathbb{GL}_{d+1}(K)$.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dospinescu, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}

item.title: The Pila-Zannier strategy for Drinfeld modules and Drinfeld modular curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.19952v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the Pila-Zannier strategy to Drinfeld modules: we prove analogues of the Manin-Mumford theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modules of equal rank, and of the Andr\'e-Oort theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modular curves. In characteristic zero, several steps of this strategy rest on $o$-minimality, which has no counterpart over a function field; we replace the counting step by the rigid analytic Pila-Wilkie theorem of Binyamini-Kato, and this appears to be its first arithmetic application. The functional transcendence input, namely an analogue of the Ax-Lindemann theorem in both settings, is established here by an independent point counting argument.
item.dc:creator: Gal Binyamini, Dmitry Novikov, Francesco Maria Saettone

item.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.03100v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.
item.dc:creator: Noriyuki Otsubo

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and is no longer asymptotically ordered by powers of $1/g$ when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$, uniform in $n\ge0$. For $n\ge1$, its coefficients are analytic in a density parameter on a neighborhood of a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its explicit leading term contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at a sufficiently small multiple of $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\mathrm{e}^{-a\sqrt g})$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the asymptotic profiles of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotic ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers into pure $\psi$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, determines the overall constant through Painlev\'e I without assuming that the Weil--Petersson genus expansion is resurgent, and recovers individual volumes by Gaussian and Poisson coefficient extraction. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n$ cusps tends to zero in probability whenever $n/\sqrt g\to\infty$; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Zhiyi Li, Bolin Qiu, Shuaijia Wang, Yuan Zhong, Kun Chen, Renqiu Xia
